architecture_decisions: {Architecture Decision: Implement a provider-neutral, configuration-driven model routing capability}
work_items: {Work Item: Add provider-neutral, configuration-driven model routing capability}
validations: {Validation: Protected validation and canonical model identity remain unchanged, while local-first routing is opt-in and server-owned}

AC-01: validate protected requirement — With no local-first configuration, effective runtime order remains exactly `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, and existing hosted transport tests remain green.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — A bounded server-owned configuration can place one admitted local model before the hosted chain. Empty, duplicate, malformed, unsupported, caller-controlled or secret-bearing route configuration fails closed before model execution.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — A configured local endpoint applies only to its admitted local route. Hosted GPT-5.6 routes continue to use the fixed Vercel AI Gateway endpoint with canonical model IDs and are not redirected to the local endpoint.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — When the local route returns a result accepted by the existing protected validator, routing returns that result and does not attempt a hosted model. Bounded attempt evidence identifies the local model/provider without exposing endpoint credentials or payloads.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — When the local route is unavailable or raises a provider failure, routing records only sanitized bounded failure evidence and advances to the next admitted hosted route without changing the acceptance contract.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — When the local route returns output rejected by the existing protected validator, routing records `validation_failed`, advances to the next admitted route and cannot lower or bypass the validator.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Request-scoped Vercel OIDC remains the only automatic hosted-production GPT-5.6 credential path. Process `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` remains non-authoritative and local configuration cannot substitute a credential for hosted production routing.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Existing `DSPY_API_BASE` / `DSPY_API_KEY` behavior remains an intentional operator override. Local-first provider configuration is not silently combined with or substituted for this compatibility path.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Logs and attempt evidence contain only admitted model/provider identity, status, duration and sanitized error class. Tests prove endpoint credentials, authorization values, raw provider errors/results and generated content are not logged.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Tests and code inspection prove local-first routing grants no shell/network capability, source acceptance, Project/spec mutation, provider spending authority, GitHub/Vercel authority, approval, REVIEW completion or production deployment authority.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — The worker branch passes authentic DSPy spec compilation, protected `--require-dspy` plan validation and applicable exact-head Workstream Spec Validation, Bounded Autonomy Pilot and P2 CI. The PR remains draft/DO NOT MERGE and no deployment occurs.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Before integration, Wave 6 is deployment-verified and `CURRENT-STATE.md` reconciled; this branch is rebased/reconciled to that exact production SHA, architecture drift is resolved, required authentic evidence and exact-head gates are rerun, and Control Tower explicitly authorizes integration.
risks: {Risk: No material risk, but potential for local-first configuration failure or unavailability of admitted routes, which may advance to the next admitted route without changing acceptance requirements}
